title: Existence of an integer median of an integer-valued function (Simon 5.1, (31))
statement: Let α be a type with a σ-algebra and μ a measure on it. Let F ⊆ α be measurable with μ(F) = ofReal a for a real number a > 0. Let u : α → ℝ be measurable with u(x) ∈ ℤ for every x. Then there is an integer β such that ofReal(a/2) ≤ μ(F ∩ {x : u(x) ≤ β}) and ofReal(a/2) ≤ μ(F ∩ {x : β ≤ u(x)}).
lean_statement: ∀ {α : Type} [MeasurableSpace α] (μ : Measure α) (F : Set α) (a : ℝ) (u : α → ℝ), MeasurableSet F → 0 < a → μ F = ENNReal.ofReal a → Measurable u → (∀ x, ∃ k : ℤ, u x = k) → ∃ β : ℤ, ENNReal.ofReal (a / 2) ≤ μ (F ∩ {x | u x ≤ β}) ∧ ENNReal.ofReal (a / 2) ≤ μ (F ∩ {x | (β : ℝ) ≤ u x})
